title: Better Auth 1.7 Ships the Enterprise Tier as MIT
caption:
The enterprise checklist that used to block my first real contract is now an npm install.

Better Auth 1.7 landed August 18. SCIM 2.0 provisioning, SAML assertion verification, OIDC back-channel logout, DPoP sender-constrained tokens. MIT, all of it.

Not a drop-in upgrade though. oidcProvider is deleted, accounts get rekeyed to (issuer, accountId), and you have to backfill before you deploy. Still cheaper than building SCIM.

What's blocking your enterprise deal?

slides.headline:
The enterprise tier
is now MIT.
slides.sub: Better Auth 1.7 shipped August 18 with SCIM 2.0, SAML hardening, OIDC back-channel logout and DPoP.

slides.title: Offboarding, handled
slides.sub: SCIM 2.0 inbound, RFC 7643 and 7644. Your customer's directory pushes users, groups and memberships — and revokes them.

slides.title: Logout propagates
slides.sub: OIDC back-channel logout. The IdP ends the session and your app's session dies with it.

slides.title: Stolen tokens die
slides.sub: RFC 9449. Tokens bind to the client key via cnf.jkt, and the bearer path refuses them.

slides.title: The upgrade costs you
items: oidcProvider is deleted. Your migration target is oauth-provider.
Accounts rekeyed to (issuer, accountId). Backfill before deploy.
MCP support moved out into a separate package.
Device and user codes now require unique indexes.

slides.headline:
Enterprise ready.
MIT licensed.
slides.sub: and I'll send the 1.7 migration notes
